name: Infineon Smart Power Fab Dresden

parties.name: Federal Government of Germany
parties.note: Granted the direct subsidy cleared by the European Commission; the federal economy ministry issued the final funding approval in May 2025.

parties.name: European Commission
parties.note: Approved the German aid measure under EU State aid rules and the Chips Act framework.

summary: A new front-end fab at Infineon's existing Dresden site for discrete power semiconductors and analog/mixed-signal chips on 300 mm wafers, run together with Villach as one virtual fab. Construction began with a groundbreaking in May 2023. The European Commission cleared up to €920 million of German grant aid in February 2025 and the final national approval followed in May 2025. Infineon opened the plant on 2 July 2026, months earlier than planned; the Commission expects it to reach full capacity in 2031.

location.note: Built as an expansion of Infineon's existing Dresden manufacturing site.

metrics.note: Infineon's own investment, which Infineon calls the largest single investment in its history; approximately €5 billion when first announced.
Investment amount the Commission names as supported by the German aid measure.

Direct grant approved by the Commission in February 2025, with final German funding approval in May 2025. Infineon puts total public funding for the site from the Chips Act and IPCEI ME/CT at about €1 billion.

milestones.note: Infineon's boards approved the Dresden site and the company announced the start of the project, with about €5 billion of investment planned.
Construction began early after Germany allowed a project start ahead of the state aid decision.
At the groundbreaking Infineon targeted the start of manufacturing for autumn 2026.
Opened several months ahead of schedule.
The Commission states the plant will reach full capacity in 2031.

notes: Infineon also invests in Dresden through its stake in the separate ESMC foundry joint venture, which is not part of this record. The building shell was topped out in April 2025.
